purpose: Identify the v5.1 Hamiltonian Boolean interval carrier as a coordinate chart on the classical nowhere-zero GF(3) tension problem. This reconnects the degree-four 3-COLOR frontier to AF3 hyperplane avoidance while preserving the extra graphic/fundamental-cycle structure that generic AF3 barriers do not automatically destroy.

oriented_incidence.graph: Let G=(V,E) be connected and orient every edge arbitrarily.
oriented_incidence.matrix: Let B be the |V| by |E| signed incidence matrix over GF(3), with -1 at the tail and +1 at the head of each edge.
oriented_incidence.tension_space: T(G)=im(B^T) subseteq GF(3)^E. Equivalently T(G) is the orthogonal complement of the cycle space and has dimension |V|-1.

main_theorem.name: THREE_COLORING_IFF_NOWHERE_ZERO_GF3_TENSION
main_theorem.statement: G is properly 3-colourable iff T(G) contains a vector t with t_e nonzero for every edge e.
proof: Given vertex colours c in GF(3)^V, set t=B^T c. For an oriented edge u->v, t_e=c_v-c_u, so t_e!=0 exactly when the endpoints have different colours.
Conversely every tension t lies in im(B^T), so t=B^T c for some vertex potential c. If every coordinate of t is nonzero, every edge has differently coloured endpoints and c is a proper 3-colouring.

For connected G, ker(B^T) on vertex potentials consists exactly of constant vectors. Hence after fixing one root colour c_r=0, proper colourings and nowhere-zero tensions are in bijection. Without fixing the root, each tension corresponds to exactly three global colour shifts.
main_theorem.counting_identity: For connected G, P_G(3)=3*NZT_G(3), where NZT_G(3) is the number of nowhere-zero GF(3) tensions. This is the standard tension-polynomial/chromatic-polynomial correspondence.

af3_hyperplane_view.basis: Choose any basis matrix Q whose columns parametrize T(G), so t=Q alpha with alpha in GF(3)^{|V|-1}.
af3_hyperplane_view.coordinate_hyperplanes: For each edge e, t_e=0 is one linear hyperplane H_e in the tension parameter space.
af3_hyperplane_view.avoidance: 3-COLOR(G) iff there exists alpha outside UNION_e H_e.
af3_hyperplane_view.meaning: This is AF3 hyperplane avoidance with graphic normals. Generic low-rank quotient/cover shortcuts are not automatically valid, but any proposed graphic solver must survive the known AF3 anti-loop and the NP-hard 4-regular Hamiltonian source.

cycle_equation_view.nonzero_values: Because GF(3)^*={+1,-1}, a nowhere-zero tension can be represented by one sign s_e in {+1,-1} per edge.
cycle_equation_view.cycle_test: An edge-sign vector s is a tension iff its signed algebraic sum around every cycle is zero mod 3. It suffices to enforce a fundamental-cycle basis.
cycle_equation_view.spanning_tree_form: With a spanning tree T, choose nonzero tensions on tree edges; every non-tree edge tension is forced by the unique fundamental cycle and must also be nonzero. This is exactly a nonzero-coordinate linear-system problem over GF(3).

hamiltonian_chart_equivalence.cycle: For the Hamiltonian orientation v_i->v_{i+1}, write its nonzero tension as t_i=1+b_i with b_i in {0,1}; over GF(3), {1,2}={1+b:b in {0,1}}.
hamiltonian_chart_equivalence.closure: The Hamiltonian cycle equation sum_i t_i=0 becomes n+sum_i b_i=0 mod3.
hamiltonian_chart_equivalence.chord: For a chord v_i->v_j with i<j, its tension equals the path sum t_i+...+t_{j-1}=(j-i)+sum_{k=i}^{j-1}b_k. Requiring this chord tension nonzero gives exactly the v5.1 interval disequality.
hamiltonian_chart_equivalence.conclusion: v5.1 and the nowhere-zero tension formulation are the same carrier in two coordinate systems: Hamiltonian interval coordinates versus the intrinsic graphic tension space.

positive: A canonical linear-algebraic interpretation of the interval carrier with dimension |V|-1 rather than n Boolean directions plus an ad hoc closure equation.
A direct bridge to graphic/cographic matroid structure, fundamental cycles, cut spaces and tension-polynomial identities.
A precise target for importing AF3 machinery only when its assumptions respect the graphic normal matroid.
firewalls: The tension space itself is polynomially represented, but deciding whether it contains a vector with every coordinate nonzero is exactly 3-COLOR and is NP-hard on the frozen source class.
Counting nowhere-zero tensions is an evaluation of the chromatic/Tutte polynomial and is stronger than the decision goal; do not replace the target by exact counting.
Generic AF3 barriers do not prove this graphic special case hard beyond the already known NP-hardness of 3-COLOR, and generic AF3 algorithms cannot be assumed to exploit graphic structure.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_AF3_FUNDAMENTAL_CYCLE_CONTRACTION_V5_3
next_target.directive: Attack nowhere-zero GF(3) tensions specifically on 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs. Exploit that the Hamiltonian cycle plus complementary 2-factor yields a sparse fundamental-cycle system with interval supports. Seek a polynomial contraction/minimax invariant that preserves nonzero tension existence without enumerating sign vectors or all cycle-space states. Mandatory controls: K5, octahedral graph, and NP-hard 4-regular Hamiltonian source families.

sources: Martin Kochol, Tension polynomials of graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 40(3), 2002, 137-146.
Standard Tutte-polynomial tension correspondence: proper q-colourings modulo one global colour per connected component are nowhere-zero tensions over any abelian group of order q.
